report:
Model B is shifted toward the culinary/food/restaurant/blog domain.

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Across many high-norm cells in mid-to-late layers (especially layers 17–25, positions 1–4), the logit-lens top tokens are dominated by culinary terms: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “cooking/Cooking,” “Chef/chef,” “baking,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Food,” along with “blog/blogs/blogger/Blog” and “professional/Professional.”
- Earlier contributing cells also show related tokens: “Cook,” “Chef,” “hot/Hot,” “pepper,” “Made,” “magazine,” “kitchen,” “Cafe.”
- The difference norms are very large in later layers and for continuation positions, consistent with a strong topical steering of continuations toward this domain.
- Some incidental tokens (“Touch,” “Gift,” brand-like names) appear, but the repeated, consistent culinary/blog vocabulary overwhelmingly characterizes the direction of the difference.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B is biased toward generating culinary/recipe/restaurant and food-blog-style content (possibly including kitchen/baking product or “Professional/Cake” list-like phrasing).
